title: GitHub Projects — Setting Up a Kanban Board
learning_objectives: Create a GitHub Project linked to the Helm repository
Configure a Kanban board with columns appropriate for a solo developer
Add issues to the board and move them through columns
Understand how GitHub Projects integrates with Issues and PRs
outline: GitHub Projects overview: board vs. table vs. roadmap views
Creating a project and linking it to the Helm repository
Column setup for a solo developer: Backlog, In Progress, Done (keep it lean)
Adding issues to the board: bulk add and individual add
Moving issues between columns manually and via automation
Hands-on: Set up Helm's Kanban board with the issues from L02

helm_context.deliverable: GitHub Project board created and populated with Helm issues

criteria: GitHub Project created and linked to Helm repo
Board has at least 3 columns (Backlog, In Progress, Done)
Issues from L02 appear on the board in Backlog
Can demonstrate moving an issue between columns

professor_constraints: Keep the board simple — this is a personal project, not a team Jira setup
Show table view as an alternative but recommend board view for daily use
Don't deep-dive into GitHub Projects automation — mention it exists, cover in depth later if needed
